decisions.reason: As a close-to-core rye bread using existing skills and equipment, it is inexpensive to keep as an option, though some overlap with other new bread variants creates a moderate rationalization risk.
As the firm's declared flagship seasonal product with a renewed gold medal, it has strong revealed quality and brand value, so there is little reason to abandon it.
This seeded rye mixed bread fits the established assortment well and can stay on the market at low incremental cost while demand becomes clearer.
The dark barley malt rye bread is still a low-cost extension of the bread line, but its more niche taste profile and similarity to other rye launches make it somewhat more droppable.
A marzipan stollen is a natural seasonal line extension for a German bakery-confectionery firm, and absent negative signals it is worth keeping for another season.

The ancient grain bread offers upside as a differentiated artisanal product and is cheap to continue testing, although its ingredients and positioning likely make demand somewhat less certain than for standard breads.
